supportingSources.label: Kineticist Ice-Revue / Ice Show machine guide

strategy.summary: Plunge unlit top lanes to raise bumper value, complete safe standup pairs to build both center saucers to 200, then use controlled saucer entries as scoring shots and cross-playfield transfers.

quickInfo.name: Top lanes
quickInfo.summary: Each of the five top lanes lights its corresponding bumper for 10 points instead of 1 point.

quickInfo.name: Standup targets
quickInfo.summary: Each numbered standup target lights its corresponding outlane for 50 points instead of 5 points.

quickInfo.name: Target pairs
quickInfo.summary: Completed standup-target pairs raise both center saucers from 50 to 100 and then 200 points.

quickInfo.name: Center saucers
quickInfo.summary: A successful center-saucer shot ejects the ball toward the opposite flipper.

quickInfo.name: Lower layouts
quickInfo.summary: Known playfields use either four outlanes with small slingshots or six outlanes without slingshots.

steps.text: Before each plunge, identify a top lane whose corresponding bumper is not lit.
Plunge through that top lane when the lane is reachable.
From either flipper, send controlled shots toward the top lanes.
Guide upper play toward an uncollected lane instead of a lit lane.
Shoot a numbered standup target only from a controlled ball.
Complete target pairs to raise the center saucers to 200.
Shoot a 200-point center saucer when its entry is controlled.
Drop catch or dead bounce the saucer eject on the opposite flipper.
Return to the top lanes after the saucer collect.

fallback.title: Recovery: Saucer transfer
fallback.when: Recovery pivot: Use this plan when upward shots return through dangerous bumpers or outlane dividers.

steps.text: Choose the center saucer that is reachable from the controlled flipper.
Shoot only when the ball can enter the saucer cleanly.
Track the eject toward the opposite flipper.
Control the ball, then choose another saucer or a safer upward shot.

alternatives.title: Position play: Target-pair qualification
alternatives.when: When trailing, use this distinct scoreboard route: use this plan when one controlled target hit completes a pair and raises both saucers.

steps.text: Identify the missing target in the nearest incomplete pair.
Shoot that target from the flipper with the safer rebound angle.
Stop target shots after both saucers reach 200.
Take a center saucer from control.
Collect different top lanes to light their bumpers for 10.
Complete controlled standup-target pairs.
Complete more standup-target pairs until both center saucers reach 200.
Use the center saucers as scoring shots and flipper transfers.

techniques.name: Unlit-lane plunge
techniques.instruction: Read the five bumper lamps before the plunge. Aim for a top lane whose bumper still scores 1 point.

techniques.name: Dead bounce
techniques.instruction: Dead bounce a predictable center-saucer eject to the opposite flipper when the receiving side is clear.

techniques.name: Nudging
techniques.instruction: Use small nudges while the ball contacts an outlane-divider post. Move the ball inward toward a flipper.

cautions.issue: Every unsuccessful non-saucer shot has rebound drain risk.
cautions.response: Prefer clean saucer entries and controlled upward shots. Do not shoot a standup target from a moving ball.

cautions.issue: The four-outlane layout adds small slingshots beside the flippers.
cautions.response: Read each slingshot kick before you depend on a dead bounce. Nudge before the ball reaches an outer lane.

cautions.issue: The six-outlane layout has no slingshots and leaves more divider posts exposed.
cautions.response: Nudge while the ball rattles between divider posts. Guide it inward before it enters an outlane.

checkBeforePlay: Confirm whether the game is 1965 Ice-Revue replay or 1966 Ice Show add-a-ball, and read the matching instruction card.
Confirm four- or six-outlane playfield, ball count, tilt, Special treatment, posts, slingshots, lane lamps, and saucer scoring.
Test five top lanes, numbered standups, bumpers, both center saucers, ejects, divider posts, slingshots, and every lower-lane feed.
strategy.simpleOverview: Ice-Revue uses five top lanes to light matching bumpers and standup-target pairs to raise both center saucers. Plunge an unlit lane, complete controlled target pairs until the saucers reach 200, and use each saucer as both a scoring shot and a transfer to the opposite flipper.
strategy.overview: Ice-Revue uses five top lanes to light matching bumpers and standup-target pairs to raise both center saucers. Collect different lanes to light the bumpers, complete controlled pairs until the saucers reach 200, then use the saucers for points and cross-playfield transfers. Account for the installed lower-playfield layout before trusting an outlane return.
